A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NSD/CLIP shared-decodable-concept study despite v2's shortened title. The main text, equations, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including v2's added Section 7.

before.justification: V1 reports original fMRI decoding results against ridge regression in Figure 12 and original cross-participant clustering findings in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds participant-subgroup decoding results and original caption-based analyses of the identified clusters.

M1.justification: Section 7 adds a text interpretation procedure: retrieve captions using CLIP text embeddings and positive/negative cluster centroids, then construct word clouds. The linear decoder and modified DBSCAN procedure are retained. The corrected loss formula does not establish that training implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 extends semantic analysis to natural-language captions for 73,000 NSD images, whereas v1 interprets clusters through representative images. This adds text-modality coverage within the existing stimulus collection; the eight-participant natural-image fMRI task remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 12 adds BrainCLIP, identified as Liu et al. (2023), using results reported by that work. V1 compares only with ridge regression and chance. Those existing comparators remain; v2 does not report independently retraining BrainCLIP.

E3.justification: V2 adds a comparison averaged over participants 1, 2, 5, and 7, while noting BrainCLIP's 982 test images versus this study's 1,000. Section 7 also introduces retrieval of 50 positive and 50 negative captions from 365,000 embeddings. Existing decoding splits, training settings, and clustering thresholds are retained.

E4.justification: Section 7 adds a qualitative check of whether caption words support the image-based cluster interpretations. Section 3.1 also newly reports qualitative observations about expansion, initialization averaging, and overconnection near epsilon 0.7. These supplement existing analyses without adding controlled, quantified ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 50 decoder fits per participant and standard errors across eight participants in Figure 12. V2 relocates and explains the averaging passage but introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds four-participant curves at k = 1, 5, and 10, with the proposed decoder above the cited BrainCLIP results under nonidentical test sets. Section 7 adds caption findings supporting color and lighting interpretations but offering weak support for food/softness. Existing cluster findings and the decoder-versus-ridge trend remain.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes exponentiated cosine distance in v1 to cosine similarity in v2, correcting the mathematical inconsistency with attracting matched embeddings. This is more than the accompanying loss renaming. No new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: contrastive decoding, cross-participant DBSCAN, identification of known and potentially new visual concepts, and interpretation through positive and negative representative images. The shortened title and new supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds specific discussion of stimulus-category bias, temporal resolution, and density-based merging of distinct concepts. Section 7 qualifies interpretations when captions inadequately identify hands, legs, or food/softness. The existing need for targeted hypothesis-driven validation remains.

D1.justification: V2 documents the caption-embedding and retrieval recipe and names the wordcloud Python package. Conversely, Section 6.3 removes the HCP-atlas overlay description. Existing optimizer settings, voxel counts, hardware, training times, and normalization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. (2023), BrainCLIP, as a directly reported comparison and removes Glasser et al. (2016) alongside the HCP-atlas description. The broader positioning relative to functional-localization and visual-decoding research is retained.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, updates the first author's affiliation, and locally rewrites Sections 3–3.2 to explain the existing procedure. It reorganizes Broader Impacts and Limitations and adds Section 7. The overall narrative and most results prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 12 is widened and redrawn with additional curves, an expanded legend, and caption. New Figure 20 presents word clouds; old Figures 20–21 move and become Figures 21–22. Most existing displays are retained, although some references inside the new word-cloud figure retain outdated numbers.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency in Equation 1 and makes cluster interpretations more assessable through caption-based checks and more specific limitations. The gains remain limited because the central empirical study is unchanged and no independent neural validation is added. Nonidentical BrainCLIP test sets, removed HCP-atlas documentation, and stale figure references temper but do not outweigh these improvements.
